instructions: borer is a reverse-engineering engine (Rust): borer-engine is a pure, sync analysis library, crates/borer a thin MCP server and CLI over it, app/ a GPUI desktop app. CLAUDE.md is the rule book. Report real defects with the concrete input or sequence that triggers them; no praise, no restating the change, no style nits that rustfmt, clippy, typos or ruff already enforce in the project's gate.

rules.rule: Never claim more than the engine shows: a heuristic answer names its evidence and says when it is unsure; a missed finding beats a false one.
No clock, random seed, hash-map or hash-set iteration order, or environment variable may reach an answer: the same binary and query give the same bytes at any thread count.

File bytes are hostile: every read is bounds-checked, every scan capped, every walk fuel-limited, and arithmetic on values from the file is checked, saturating or wrapping. No input may cause a panic, hang or unbounded allocation.
No unwrap, expect, panic!, unreachable! or todo! outside tests. No `let _ =` or `.ok()` that drops a Result that matters.

A test or benchmark changed only to make it pass is a defect. Every fix comes with a test: decompiler fixes under tests/it/decompile/, lifter fixes as an *_agrees_with_the_emulator test, a parser crash input in tests/hostile.rs.

borer-engine stays pure: no async, tokio, MCP types, filesystem writes or global state; memoized results go through Analysis::derived (get_or_build), never a second Mutex map; per-function parallel work uses std::thread::scope with results in address order, never rayon.
No integer `as` casts: width conversions use num::lo32, cast_signed, cast_unsigned, u64::from, try_from or num::as_f64.
Match borer's own enums exhaustively; a wildcard arm is allowed only over a foreign enum.
No `//` or `/* */` comments except `// SAFETY:` above an unsafe block and `// ASM:` on hand-assembled bytes; explanations belong in rustdoc. unsafe appears only in crates/borer-live and tests.
No `#[allow(...)]`; a silenced lint is `#[expect(lint, reason = "...")]` on the one site.

The server is a thin adapter: logic belongs in the engine. stdout is the MCP protocol, so nothing else prints to it. Every list is a plain table with a `#` header line, takes filter, offset, limit and count, and is hard-capped with `showing N of M`. A failing handler returns ErrorData, never error text inside a success. A state-changing tool is a dry run by default.

borer-app formats the engine's tokens and never derives a fact of its own; no engine call on the UI thread; every edit goes through the agents' edit path. The main workspace under crates/ never depends on a GPL crate.

Each commit holds one concern. Commit and PR titles are `type: summary`: lowercase, imperative, plain ASCII, at most 72 characters, no scope, no trailing period; type is one of add, fix, improve, refactor, perf, docs, test, chore, revert.
